chapter: Las Vegas, Sinatra and later years
title: Hearing loss and the ear operation
summary: In Palm Springs he realized his hearing was failing, had an operation, and thought he'd never play again.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: And then after I had the ear problem, that I was down in Palm Springs,
-- and I had the operation and I thought 'Well, I'll never play again, and I guess I can tell you about how I got back in playing. I had really give up the idea that I'd ever play again.
Well, you know, you didn't say -- you didn't say exactly --
Well a lot of people ask me, they'll say ask -- I don't like to tell these things, I suppose, but I suppose --
-- some people would like to know. It -- it was getting bad. I knew it. When I worked here at the Rainbow room, I knew something was happening --
Things -- sometimes nights it would all right, and some nights would be funny things, would be funny --
So, in Palm Springs, I knew it was there and found I was playing -- I Concentrate On You and I -- I'd never looked down when I play, and I realized I was -- what was

So I packed up that night and I told the men I had to go home. And I did. So I started examining and found -- finally had an operation, but in a month after I went home I couldn't hear anything. I couldn't hear the telephone, I couldn't hear on the telephone. Anybody called, and it was really quite a depressing time for me.

But Eve was a gem through it all, and I found I had an operation and it helped. And I had a slight cold. I had the operation in April and I went -- went up in June and stayed with a drummer friend of mine in Vegas, cause it was real hot at that time, it was 110 at that time, it was one of those years when it was hot that (unintelligible).
